EXCAVATION

Excavation Near Utilities: Information That Must Reach the Tender Team

Buried and overhead services are critical planning interfaces.

In this insight

Utilities belong in the initial briefIdentify who controls each interfaceAsk how uncertainty affects the offerMaintain a current information setFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Utilities belong in the initial brief

Service information should reach the project team before excavation planning is treated as settled. Record the available utility drawings, surveys and known constraints, while distinguishing records from verified site information. The relevant competent specialists must determine the investigation and protection approach. The client can support that process by making the information accessible and assigning clear responsibility for unresolved enquiries.

Identify who controls each interface

A service may involve the owner, an authority, a designer and more than one contractor. Create an interface schedule showing who can authorise diversions, isolation, protection or access. Do not assume that the excavation contractor can resolve every dependency independently. Authority response periods and third-party permissions may need explicit places in the programme.

Ask how uncertainty affects the offer

Tenderers should explain how incomplete service information influences their assumptions, allowances and proposed sequence. Compare these qualifications before award. Where further investigation is needed, define how it will be commissioned and how its findings will be incorporated into the scope. This is more useful than accepting a general exclusion and discovering later that the principal work area is unavailable.

Maintain a current information set

As investigations and diversions progress, update the shared records and brief affected teams. Keep a clear revision history so superseded information is not mistaken for current guidance. Document unresolved questions and required approvals. The aim is a controlled handover of service information into the excavation package, with no implication that a historic drawing alone establishes a safe method of work.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Distinguish utility records from verified information.
  • Assign third-party approvals and diversions.
  • Keep service updates within document control.

  • Further reading: HSE — Excavations (UK guidance)
